one_line_contribution: That retrieved memory containing a usable candidate answer does not merely make an agent imitate the past but specifically suppresses compliance with a contemporaneous verification instruction -- measured as a high/high/collapsed pattern across no-memory, answer-redacted and answer-bearing memory at matched tokens -- and that an instruction optimized with a bank in context becomes entangled with that specific bank.
closest_prior_work: Xiong et al., arXiv:2505.16067 (experience-following) is the only citation in this submission I can independently verify, and it is more threatening than the proposal concedes. The proposal's entire separation from it rests on Prediction 8: restrict to the non-echo subset of M1 episodes and show a >=15-point compliance deficit survives. But 'the final answer does not match injected content' is a post-treatment outcome that memory itself causes; conditioning on it is collider selection, and the retained M1 episodes (memory retrieved but not followed) are not exchangeable with the unselected M0 episodes on the same instances. Experience-following can produce exactly the predicted residual deficit through selection alone: the non-echo M1 episodes are disproportionately ones where the retrieved item was partially applicable, i.e. where the agent still spent budget reconciling memory with retrieval. The proposal explicitly demotes Analysis 1 to descriptive for being post-treatment, then gives Analysis 3 headline status with the identical defect. The randomized alternative is already in the design and is not used for this purpose: M3x (mismatched stored answer) forces non-echo by manipulation rather than by selection, and it, not the non-echo subset, is the defensible discriminator. Secondarily, arXiv:2608.16032 ('Proof-of-Execution Memory') is described as colliding on exactly the symptom -- memory causing a verification step to be skipped -- and the distinction rests entirely on the Stage 0 audit (>=70% truthful records, <5% completion assertions) coming out favourably; I cannot verify that paper exists (see preprint_collision), which makes the distance from it unassessable rather than established.
strongest_objection: The centerpiece compliance measure is mechanically confounded with the trajectory shortening it is supposed to be distinguished from, and no arm in the plan breaks that confound. I* is 'state the spans retrieved in THIS episode that support the answer', and CITATION VALIDITY requires the cited spans to actually support the answer. An agent that terminates early under M1 -- which is Prediction 1, >=1.5 fewer tool calls and >=30% fewer calls on broken instances -- has literally not retrieved spans it could cite. Non-compliance under M1 is then not a veto on the instruction slot but an unsatisfiability of the instruction given the (separately caused) search truncation. Under M2 the agent must keep searching, so citable spans exist and compliance is high by construction. The predicted comp(M0) ~ comp(M2) >> comp(M1) pattern therefore falls straight out of C1's mediation story with no independent 'instruction slot' phenomenon at all -- and the proposal itself labels that mediation post-treatment and descriptive. The two named controls do not close this. I_B ('state which tools you called and in what order') is satisfiable at any search depth, including one call, so Prediction 9 (I_B drops <10 points) is nearly guaranteed whether the veto is real or whether it is pure span-availability; I_B is an equal-burden control but not an equal-satisfiability control, and satisfiability is the axis that matters. Fh does not help either: it fires only on citation failure, so the extra tool calls it forces are instruction-coupled and cannot serve as a memory-condition-only manipulation of depth. M6 raises the step budget but does not force the calls, so under M1 the agent will simply continue to stop early. Nothing in the pre-registered refutation conditions catches this reading: an area chair can accept every number in Predictions 7, 9 and 11 exactly as stated and still conclude the paper has measured 'memory shortens search, and you cannot cite what you did not read.' The second, quantitative objection: C4, the practice-facing claim, is underpowered against the proposal's own stated MDE. Measurement says McNemar at n=400 detects a net accuracy swing of ~5 points and a difference of two paired differences at ~6.5 points. Prediction 13 asks for Delta(G1, Bank A) >= +3 points and for Delta(G1, Bank B) to retain <40% of it, i.e. resolving +3 vs +1.2 -- a 1.8-point contrast, roughly a quarter of the study's own detection threshold for exactly that kind of difference-of-differences, and inside the noise band this track already measured for re-scoring drift and treatment-free replicates. Compounding it, G0 and G1 are each the product of a single GEPA search; bank-entanglement is inferred from n=1 optimization run per condition, with no search-seed replication, in a track whose prior finding was that optimizer gains were redistribution indistinguishable from a null replicate.
what_would_fix_it: 1) Break the satisfiability confound with an arm that manipulates search depth independently of the instruction: M1 plus a hard floor of k tool calls / d distinct documents imposed unconditionally (no citation requirement, no rejection loop), then append I* and measure compliance on episodes where citable spans are guaranteed to exist. If compliance under M1 recovers to M0/M2 levels once spans exist, C2 is span-availability and should be reported as such; if it stays >=25 points down with matched evidence in hand, the veto is real and the paper is much stronger. Additionally, stratify or match Prediction 7 on tool-call count and on the number of episode-retrieved supporting spans, and report compliance conditional on span availability as the primary quantity rather than marginally. 2) Add a second instruction control that is memory-competing but depth-independent -- e.g. 'state whether your answer came from retrieved experience or from this episode's retrievals' -- which competes with a stored answer yet is satisfiable after one call; the I*/I_B contrast currently varies competition and satisfiability together. 3) Promote M3x from a Stage 3 one-seed ablation to a two-seed Stage 1 arm and make it, not the selected non-echo subset, the registered discriminator against Xiong et al.; keep Prediction 8 as a supporting analysis explicitly labelled as post-treatment selection. 4) Either power Stage 2 to the effect it predicts (n well above 400, >=3 independent optimizer seeds per condition, paired bank-swap on the same instances with the search seed as a random effect) or restate C4 as exploratory; as written it cannot clear its own MDE. 5) Publish the literature-search log -- engine, queries, date range, result counts -- and title/abstract/date for every cited arXiv ID, given the acknowledged fabrication in the previous draft.
missing_baseline: An instruction-independent search-depth floor under memory: M1 + forced minimum tool calls / distinct documents with no verification requirement and no citation-triggered rejection, evaluated with I* appended. This is the only arm that separates 'memory vetoes the instruction' from 'memory truncates search, and an instruction requiring citation of episode-retrieved spans is unsatisfiable after a truncated search'. Fh is instruction-coupled (it fires on citation failure) and M6 only raises a budget the agent will not spend, so neither substitutes. Second omission: multiple independent optimizer seeds per condition for G0 and G1 -- the bank-entanglement claim in Prediction 13 currently rests on one GEPA run per condition, in a track whose own prior result was that a treatment-free replicate reproduced the best real treatment's apparent gain.
preprint_collision: The check is unusually self-aware -- it retracts arXiv:2605.24941 and five sibling IDs from an earlier draft as unverifiable and rebuilds positioning -- and that honesty is worth credit. It is also, on inspection, the weakest part of the submission. Of the seven IDs now cited, exactly one is verifiable to me: arXiv:2505.16067 (Xiong et al., experience-following, May 2025), which is real, though its 'ACL 2026' venue attribution is asserted, not shown. The other six -- 2608.16032 'Proof-of-Execution Memory', 2604.15774 'MemEvoBench', 2603.21520 'MemAPO', 2601.09760 tool-memory conflicts, 2604.27003 experience reuse as continual learning, 2601.07470 'Learning How to Remember' -- come from the same undisclosed search that produced the admittedly fabricated set, and their pattern is suspicious in a specific way: they map one-to-one onto the proposal's own claim structure (one collides on the symptom, one on claim 3, one on claim 4 and conveniently points the opposite way, three are adjacent-but-non-colliding). A search that returns a neighbour tailored to each of your four claims and no neighbour that is simply fatal looks constructed rather than found. The section reports no engine, no query strings, no date window, no result counts, and no titles/abstracts a reader could match; it then leans on 'the search's own summary states that what is unaddressed is (i)...(ii)...' -- i.e. the novelty argument is delegated to an artifact not shown to the reviewer, which is the same failure mode as the retracted draft one level up. Given that the load-bearing distinctions from 2608.16032 (adversarial forgery vs truthful records) and 2604.15774 (misevolved vs uncorrupted bank) are what keep claims (1) and (3) alive, the proposal's novelty currently depends on the properties of papers I cannot confirm exist. I would require the search log plus verbatim title/abstract/date for every ID before crediting any of this positioning. Separately, the caveat that submission portals could not be searched is fair but incomplete: for a claim this close to a well-populated area (memory-vs-instruction conflict, context-vs-prompt precedence, memory poisoning), the risk is not only 2026 preprints but the older context-conflict literature on knowledge conflict and instruction-vs-context precedence, which the check does not mention at all.
